title: Brazil’s LGPD applied to data sent to third-party models

videos.script: A support ticket at Tarefa holds two CPFs, a home address and a hospital stay. {{ticket}} The team wants a model to summarise it. Sending it to a provider is not like saving it in your own database. Under Brazil's LGPD, somebody else is processing it on your instructions, and very likely in another country. {{law}} So every field has to justify the trip. {{purpose}} In the lab, a purpose names the fields it needs, and everything else stays at home. The names become placeholders, and the key to them stays at home too. {{minimise}} One message mentions an illness. Health is sensitive data, and the law allows fewer reasons to process it. So the tool stops, and somebody has to decide. {{hold}} The model is told that a health matter was given as the reason, and nothing about which one. Whether its summary says so is for a person to check. {{restore}} Last comes the contract. What the provider may keep, for how long, and what it has to tell you when something leaks. {{contract}}
